fields.meta_title: Pre Order Form Builder for Small-Batch Sellers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a pre order form that shows the ship date, caps the first batch and charges cards when the run is confirmed. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Pre Order Form for Products That Ship Later
fields.hero_description: Describe what you sell, when it ships and how buyers pay. Emergent builds the pre order form, counts each order against your batch and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Pre-Order Has to Promise
fields.features_subheading: A buyer paying for something that does not exist yet is owed a ship date, and a straight answer when that date moves.
fields.feature_1:
A ship date on the form and the receipt

Show the expected ship date beside the price and repeat it in the confirmation email. The order row keeps that date as well, ready for the day a buyer writes in to ask.
fields.feature_2:
Payment timed to the product

Connect Stripe and take the whole price at checkout, or a deposit now and the balance at shipping. A saved card can also wait, uncharged, until the run is confirmed.
fields.feature_3:
Caps on a limited first batch

Set how many units the first batch holds. Each order takes the next number in line, and once the batch is gone the form closes or moves buyers on to the second batch.
fields.feature_4:
A minimum before production starts

Set the order count a run needs before it goes ahead. Buyers see how close the run is on the form itself, and you get an alert the moment the count crosses your number.
fields.feature_5:
Delay notices sent to every buyer

Edit the ship date once and every open pre-order hears about it, with a choice to stay in line or back out of the order. Each buyer's answer is saved on the order it belongs to.
fields.feature_6:
Code and domain stay yours

Publish the pre-order page on your own domain or embed it in your store. Export the full source to GitHub when a developer needs to wire it into your inventory system.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Sellers Taking Orders Before Launch
fields.tab_content_1:
Each of the first 200 copies is signed

Cinderpath Press is publishing a debut novel in hardcover at $28, and the author will sign 200 copies. The form numbers pre-orders as they arrive, and the earliest buyers get the signed copies. Order 201 still goes through at the same price. It is marked for the unsigned edition, and the buyer sees that before paying.
fields.tab_content_2:
Once the run hits 150, every card is charged

Quarry Supply Co. will not cut fabric for a hoodie run under 150 units. Buyers pick a size and save a card at $68, and nobody is charged until the count reaches 150. This run closed at 163. The cards were charged that night, and the factory got one line per size: 24 small, 51 medium, 56 large and 32 extra large.
fields.tab_content_3:
One turkey count per weight goes to the farm

Holloway Butchers sells out of fresh turkeys every Thanksgiving and now takes pre-orders with a $25 deposit. Customers choose a weight class and a pickup day. Orders close on November 14. That morning the farm receives 105 birds split by weight: 18 at 10-12 lb, 41 at 14-16 lb, 33 at 18-20 lb, and 13 at 22-24 lb.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every buyer hears about the new ship date

Tessel Audio promised its $149 desk speaker for May 12, then a parts delay pushed shipping to June 9. One edit to the ship date sent all 312 pre-order buyers an email with the new date and two buttons: Keep my order and Cancel. Cancellations are refunded through Stripe, and every reply is saved on the buyer's order.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Pre Order Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the date and the payment rule before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Set a ship date you can keep
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the minimum for a run
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write the ship date down first, and pick one you can meet with room to spare. Under the FTC's Mail Order Rule, a seller needs a reasonable basis for any shipping time it states. The date goes on the form and on every order row.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Take the whole price up front when the product is certain. Take a deposit when the final cost could still move. If the run depends on reaching a minimum, save the card and charge it later. Say on the form which rule applies.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what happens when the first batch runs out. The form can close, or it can keep taking orders for a second batch with a later date. Name the cutoff number before you share the link, and tell buyers which batch they are in.
fields.howto_step_4_des: If a run only makes sense above a certain count, set that number and a closing date. Buyers see the running total, and you get an alert when it passes. If the window closes short, the saved cards are never charged.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the product, its price, the promised date, and how buyers pay into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the pre order form, the orders table and the Stripe connection. Ask for changes the same way, such as a second color.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Draft the message buyers get if the date moves before you need it. It should give the new date and a one-line reason, with a link to keep or cancel the order. Editing the ship date later sends it to every open order.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Order your own product with a Stripe test card, then open the orders table and check the order number and the promised date on the new row. Move the ship date to watch the delay email arrive. Delete the test row before launch.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Formaloo, Formplus), Pinterest boards of printable sheets and a Facebook thread on Google Forms. All of them treat a pre-order like any other order. A pre-order is a sale of something that does not exist yet, so the form has to carry what a normal order form does not: the ship date, a cap on a limited first batch, a minimum run before anyone is charged, and a way to tell every buyer when the date moves. This page shows four sellers running those mechanics.
tab_stories: A small press numbers the first 200 hardcover pre-orders as signed copies in the order they arrive, and order 201 onward ships unsigned.
